name: Input Validation
description: Input validation — sanitize user input, parameterized queries, allow-lists, server-side validation
content:
# Input Validation Rules

- Validate all user input on the server — client-side validation is for UX only, never rely on it for security
- Use parameterized queries or prepared statements for all database operations — never concatenate user input into SQL strings
- Prefer allow-lists over deny-lists — define what is permitted rather than trying to block every dangerous input
- Sanitize HTML output to prevent XSS — use context-appropriate encoding (HTML entities, URL encoding, JavaScript escaping)
- Validate input length, type, format, and range — reject requests that do not match expected schemas before processing
- Use schema validation libraries (Zod, Joi, Pydantic, JSON Schema) to define and enforce input contracts
- Reject unexpected fields — do not blindly pass user input to database queries or internal APIs (mass assignment protection)
- Validate file uploads — check MIME type, file extension, file size, and scan content. Never trust the client-reported content type
- Normalize Unicode input before validation — prevents bypass attacks using homoglyphs or encoding tricks
- Log validation failures with request context for monitoring — detect and alert on patterns that suggest automated attacks
